newsitem.title: UK: British-Borneo buys into Nirvana from BP.
newsitem.headline: British-Borneo buys into Nirvana from BP.

text.p: British-Borneo Petroleum Syndicate Plc said on Tuesday it had agree to buy into a deep water oil prospect in the Gulf of Mexico in a pact with prospect operator BP Exploration and Oil Inc, part of British Petroleum.

"Under the agreement BB will earn a 40 percent working interest by paying a disproportionate share of costs, subject to an agreed maximum cost cap on the next Nirvana well, which will be drilled by BP in early 1997," British Borneo said in a statement.
It gave no financial details of the transaction.
British Borneo will will also earn a 40 percent working interest in the offset Mississippi Canyon block 117, which contains a separate exploration prospect.

Nirvana is located 15 miles south of BP's Pompano platform and in water depths between 3,300 and 3,800 feet. Borneo said two wells have already been drilled on Nirvana and a third is required to determine if a commercial level of reserves exists.
"We are delighted to have concluded this, our first transaction with BP in the Gulf of Mexico," the statement quoted BB chief executive Alan Gaynor as saying.
"This well should tell us in a fairly short space of time whether we have been able to add another development candidate to our growing deepwater portfolio," he added.
In another buoyant day on the London stock market for oil related stocks British Borneo shares were up 45 pence, or 5.6 percent, at a year high of 847-1/2 pence by 1400 GMT
